plan: My private value is $10, which means winning is only profitable if I pay less than $10. Given the random nature of bidding, I'll aim to bid strategically around my value. Since the second-highest bid determines payment and I want to maximize profit, I'll bid slightly above my value to increase win probability while ensuring potential profit if I win. A bid of $11-$12 seems reasonable, balancing risk and potential gain.

My private value is $30. My goal is to maximize potential profit. Since this is a first-price sealed bid auction with payment of second-highest bid, I want to bid strategically. I'll bid close to, but slightly below my true value to capture potential profit. A bid around $25-$28 allows me some margin of safety. This gives me a chance to win if other bidders bid lower, while protecting against overpaying. Without knowing other bidders' values, a moderate bid near my value seems prudent.

My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. This means bidding $25 ensures I only win if the prize is worth more to me than what others will pay. If I win, I'll pay less than my bid. If I lose, I miss potential profit. With no prior history and a single round, a true-value bid maximizes my expected outcome.
